subject.title: refactor(daemon): split Windows task scheduler integration

question: Should this protected Windows daemon refactor require an after-fix Windows lifecycle capture before merge, or is there an explicit maintainer basis to waive that proof gate?
rationale: The branch changes compatibility-sensitive daemon control paths and currently supplies tests and CI rather than an observed Windows Task Scheduler or Startup fallback result; the `maintainer` label requires an explicit human decision.

options.title: Require Windows lifecycle proof
options.body: Request a redacted terminal capture, recording, or runtime log from the exact head showing the changed Scheduler and fallback lifecycle behavior before merge.

options.title: Explicitly waive the proof gate
options.body: A maintainer may document why existing focused Windows coverage is sufficient for this behavior-neutral refactor and accept the remaining runtime risk.

recommendation.title: Require Windows lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Request a redacted terminal capture, recording, or runtime log from the exact head showing the changed Scheduler and fallback lifecycle behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current PR author has the most direct context on the intended behavior-neutral split and its stated validation, though current-main ownership history was not available in the supplied evidence.
